content: Obesity is a medical condition characterized by an excessive accumulation of energy reserves in the form of fat stored within the adipose tissue of humans and other mammals. This accumulation reaches a level where it is associated with various health complications or an increased risk of mortality. Although obesity is recognized as an individual clinical condition, it is increasingly regarded as a significant and growing public health issue. Excessive body weight has been demonstrated to predispose individuals to a range of diseases, particularly cardiovascular diseases, type 2 diabetes mellitus, sleep apnea, and osteoarthritis. Obesity is defined as a state of excessive adipose tissue mass, with an abnormal increase in fat deposition within the subcutaneous connective tissue. The condition is typically assessed using the Body Mass Index (BMI), a widely accepted metric. A high BMI is strongly correlated with an elevated risk of developing potentially life-threatening medical conditions. Blood tests may be conducted to evaluate for underlying thyroid dysfunction or hormonal imbalances that could contribute to weight gain.
